subject: Machine Design
summary: design for static loading with the theories of failure (Rankine, Tresca, von Mises), stress concentration and notch sensitivity, fluctuating stresses, the endurance limit and its modifying factors, the S-N diagram, Soderberg, Goodman and Gerber criteria, and Miner's rule for cumulative damage

questions.text: In the σ1–σ2 plane, the safe (non-yielding) region predicted by the maximum shear stress (Tresca) theory for plane stress is bounded by
solution: Concept: Tresca: yielding when the largest of |σ1|, |σ2| and |σ1 − σ2| reaches Syt.
In the first and third quadrants the limit is |σ1| = Syt or |σ2| = Syt (square edges); in the second and fourth quadrants it is |σ1 − σ2| = Syt (inclined lines). Together they form a hexagon.
The von Mises locus σ1² − σ1σ2 + σ2² = Syt² is an ellipse that passes through all six corners of the hexagon; Rankine gives a square.
Exam tip: The largest gap between Tresca and von Mises is in pure shear (σ1 = −σ2): 0.5 Syt versus 0.577 Syt.

questions.text: A point on the surface of a shaft has a bending stress of 80 MPa and a torsional shear stress of 60 MPa. The material has S<sub>yt</sub> = 300 MPa. The factor of safety by the von Mises theory (round off to two decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: For σy = 0, the von Mises stress is σe = √(σ² + 3τ²).
Exam tip: Tresca would use √(σ² + 4τ²) = 144.2 MPa, giving N = 2.08. Read carefully which theory the question asks for.

questions.text: A cast-iron bracket (brittle, S<sub>ut</sub> = 200 MPa) has, at its critical point, a normal stress of 40 MPa and a shear stress of 30 MPa. The factor of safety by the maximum principal stress theory (round off to two decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: Brittle materials fail when the largest principal stress reaches Sut (Rankine theory).
Exam tip: Use Rankine (or Coulomb-Mohr) for brittle materials and von Mises/Tresca for ductile ones. GATE often tests just this choice.

questions.text: For a ductile material in pure shear, the ratio of the shear yield strength predicted by the maximum shear stress theory to that predicted by the von Mises theory is
solution: Concept: Tresca: Ssy = 0.5 Syt. von Mises: Ssy = Syt/√3 = 0.577 Syt.
Exam tip: So Tresca is up to about 13 % conservative compared with von Mises; 1.155 is the inverse ratio.

questions.text: A solid shaft transmits a torque of 1000 N·m and carries a bending moment of 800 N·m. It is made of steel with S<sub>yt</sub> = 320 MPa. Using the von Mises theory and a factor of safety of 2, the minimum diameter (in mm, round off to one decimal place) is ______
solution: Concept: σ = 32M/πd³, τ = 16T/πd³; von Mises: √(σ² + 3τ²) = (32/πd³)√(M² + ¾T²) = Syt/N.
Equivalent moment √(M² + 0.75T²) = √(800² + 0.75 × 1000²) = 1179.0 N·m
Allowable stress = 320/2 = 160 MPa
Exam tip: Tresca uses √(M² + T²) instead of √(M² + 0.75T²), so it always gives a slightly larger shaft.

questions.text: A notched specimen has a theoretical stress concentration factor of 2.5. Fatigue tests show that its endurance limit is 1/2.05 of that of an unnotched specimen. The notch sensitivity of the material (round off to two decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: Kf = (endurance limit unnotched)/(endurance limit notched) and Kf = 1 + q(Kt − 1).
Kf = 2.05
Exam tip: q lies between 0 (no notch effect) and 1 (full theoretical effect). It rises with the notch radius and with material strength.

questions.text: Which of the following treatments increases the fatigue strength of a steel spring?
opts: Decarburisation of the surface during heat treatment
solution: Concept: Fatigue cracks start at the surface under tensile stress.
Shot peening leaves a layer of compressive residual stress that delays crack initiation and raises fatigue strength.
Chromium plating leaves tensile residual stress and micro-cracks; decarburisation softens the surface; rough machining adds stress raisers. All three lower it.
Exam tip: Other beneficial treatments: surface rolling, nitriding, case carburising, polishing.

questions.text: A steel component has S<sub>ut</sub> = 600 MPa. Surface factor = 0.78, size factor = 0.85, reliability factor = 0.868 (95 %), and the fatigue stress concentration factor is 1.6 (applied to the endurance limit). Taking S<sub>e</sub>' = 0.5 S<sub>ut</sub>, the corrected endurance limit (in MPa, round off to one decimal place) is ______
solution: Concept: Marin equation Se = ka kb kc kd Se', where the notch factor is kd = 1/Kf.
Exam tip: Apply Kf either to the endurance limit or to the alternating stress, never to both.

questions.text: A 20 mm diameter rod is under an axial tensile load that varies between 10 kN and 40 kN. Its corrected endurance limit is 180 MPa and S<sub>ut</sub> = 540 MPa. The factor of safety by the Goodman criterion (round off to two decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: Goodman: σa/Se + σm/Sut = 1/N.
A = π/4 × 20² = 314.16 mm². P<sub>m</sub> = 25 kN, P<sub>a</sub> = 15 kN
σm = 79.58 MPa, σa = 47.75 MPa
Exam tip: Always split the load into mean and amplitude first; σmax alone tells you nothing in fatigue.

questions.text: A tie rod carries a steady axial load of 30 kN plus a completely reversed axial load of ±20 kN. The corrected endurance limit is 200 MPa and S<sub>yt</sub> = 350 MPa. Using the Soderberg criterion with a factor of safety of 2, the minimum rod diameter (in mm, round off to two decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: Soderberg: σa/Se + σm/Syt = 1/N with σ = P/A.
Exam tip: Soderberg is the usual choice when the question gives Syt and asks for a 'safe' design; Goodman needs Sut.

questions.text: The figure shows three fatigue failure lines on the σ<sub>m</sub>–σ<sub>a</sub> diagram. Line 2 (straight, from S<sub>e</sub> to S<sub>ut</sub>) is the
solution: Concept: All three start at Se on the σa axis; they differ in where and how they meet the σm axis.
Line 1 (straight, ends at Syt) = Soderberg; Line 2 (straight, ends at Sut) = Goodman; Curve 3 (parabola to Sut) = Gerber.
Exam tip: Langer's line runs from Syt on one axis to Syt on the other and checks yielding in the first cycle.

questions.text: A steel has S<sub>ut</sub> = 900 MPa and a corrected endurance limit of 400 MPa at 10⁶ cycles. Assuming a straight S-N line on log-log axes from 0.9 S<sub>ut</sub> at 10³ cycles to S<sub>e</sub> at 10⁶ cycles, the fatigue strength for a life of 10⁵ cycles (in MPa, round off to one decimal place) is ______
solution: Concept: On log-log axes, log S falls linearly with log N between (10³, 0.9Sut) and (10⁶, Se).
0.9 Sut = 810 MPa. From 10³ to 10⁵ is 2 of the 3 decades.
Exam tip: Check your answer lies between Se and 0.9Sut, and closer to Se the larger N is.

questions.text: A crane hook sees a repeating block of loading: 100 cycles at stress σ1 (life 5 × 10⁴ cycles), 1000 cycles at σ2 (life 5 × 10⁵ cycles) and 10 000 cycles at σ3, which is below the endurance limit. By Miner's rule, the number of blocks to failure is ______
solution: Concept: Miner's rule: failure when Σ ni/Ni = 1. Stresses below the endurance limit cause no damage (N = ∞).
Blocks to failure = 1/0.004 = 250
Exam tip: The order in which the stress levels are applied does not matter in Miner's rule; that is its main limitation.

questions.text: A stress that varies from zero to a maximum value σ<sub>max</sub> and back to zero (repeated stress, stress ratio R = 0) has
solution: Concept: σm = (σmax + σmin)/2 and σa = (σmax − σmin)/2.
With σmin = 0: σm = σa = σmax/2.
Exam tip: R = −1 is completely reversed (σm = 0), R = 0 is repeated, R = 1 is static.

questions.text: The rotating stepped shaft shown has a smaller diameter of 30 mm at the fillet. For the fillet, K<sub>t</sub> = 1.8 and q = 0.9. The corrected endurance limit of the unnotched shaft material is 250 MPa. For a factor of safety of 2, the largest bending moment the shaft can carry at the fillet (in N·m, round off to one decimal place) is ______
solution: Concept: A rotating shaft under a steady bending moment sees a completely reversed bending stress, so σa = 32M/πd³ and σm = 0.
Allowable nominal stress = Se/(Kf N) = 250/(1.72 × 2) = 72.67 MPa
Exam tip: Use the smaller diameter at the fillet, because that is where the nominal stress is calculated for Kt.
